finding.claim: Unanchored suffix allowlist (host.endswith("example.com")) lets an attacker name a host like evilexample.com; the server then fetches the raw attacker-supplied URL, so the request reaches an attacker-chosen external host and the attacker learns the response size.

trace.note: url: str taken from request query string, unmodified
host.endswith("example.com") check, no dot boundary; evilexample.com passes
httpx fetches the original url string, not the validated host
returns len(r.text) to caller, a response-size oracle

finding.guards_checked: No scheme restriction beyond httpx's http/https support (file:/gopher: not reachable). No private-IP/loopback/link-local check and no DNS pinning (hostname-string check only). follow_redirects defaults to False, so no redirect pivot. Response leaks only body length. ALLOWED_SUFFIX=".example.com" (line 7) is defined but unused, indicating the intended dot-bounded check was not applied. Impact is low-to-medium: reaching internal services needs internal DNS names under example.com (split-horizon), which an external attacker cannot register.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only check is the unanchored suffix test `host.endswith("example.com")` at mirror.py:13, which does not close the finding. ALLOWED_SUFFIX (line 7) is unused, and there is no scheme, private-IP, or exact-host check. follow_redirects is not set, so httpx's default of no redirects applies.
verdict.reason: The `url` query parameter (mirror.py:11) reaches `c.get(url)` (mirror.py:16) unmodified, and the suffix-only check at mirror.py:13 lets an attacker-registered host such as evilexample.com through, so the server fetches an attacker-chosen external host and returns the response length (mirror.py:17). The verdict holds, but the impact is limited: the response leaks only body length and reaching internal hosts still depends on internal DNS names under example.com.
